gates.name: Day-1 scope and exclusions
gates.closeWhen: Every EOS family is classified as Day 1, post-Day-1, pilot, or excluded; explicit exclusions are accepted.

gates.name: Commercial model
gates.closeWhen: Implementation, subscription, support, founding-customer treatment, change requests, and billable custom work are priced and accepted.

gates.name: Executed customer agreements
gates.closeWhen: Applicable subscription/service terms, implementation SOW, data/confidentiality terms, support terms, liability boundaries, termination, and data-return terms are executed.

gates.name: Data migration scope and rehearsal
gates.closeWhen: Source systems are inventoried, migration tiers and mappings are accepted, at least one repeatable rehearsal is completed, and exceptions are reconciled.
evidence: PR #1802 / ccd3f2d2 records the Lane B seeded-evidence rule and the successful B-05 canary at lane commit 2f262d38: deterministic SEEDED/SYNTHETIC source records, census/tiering/mapping fixtures, a repeatable migration dry-run harness, deterministic exception reporting, and passing targeted proofs. This materially proves the migration PROCESS can be rehearsed without waiting for a Taylor export; it does not prove Taylor's actual source data, accepted mappings, real exceptions, or Taylor acceptance, so this gate remains OPEN.

PR #1804 / d558f39d adds and sandbox-deploys EOS Data Import P1 at b533757a: CSV/XLSX staging and approved execution for Parts, Customers, Equipment, opening Inventory, and imported Service History, with 24/24 live sandbox acceptance and zero fabricated Work Orders. This materially strengthens the executable migration/rehearsal path, but import is deliberately sandbox-only and Taylor source facts, accepted mappings, real exception reconciliation, and Taylor acceptance remain outstanding.

gates.name: Opening inventory reconciliation
gates.closeWhen: Opening warehouse, bin, truck, and serialized inventory is reconciled to an accepted operational baseline and Taylor records acceptance.

gates.name: Production identities and roles
gates.closeWhen: The production user roster is reconciled and each Day-1 persona is verified at least privilege against production authorities.

gates.name: Taylor administrative self-service
gates.closeWhen: Designated Taylor EOS administrators can perform ordinary Day-1 administration without source-code changes, CLI commands, direct database edits, or Verenward engineering.
evidence: PR #1806 / 3294d835 consolidates Administration people management into one Users destination with a governed record page, trusted employee-profile edit command, per-field immutable audit events, and Change History while preserving separate security-role/account authorities.

PR #1807 verified the existing sandbox admin RoleAssignment and effective-access feed, corrected the client request set so granted Administration capabilities are actually asked of the trusted resolver, and created no new grant or production activation.

PR #1808 / 57a5ad47 live-verified Administration -> Users on platform-sandbox Hosting 8e90b41e. The running sandbox proved responsive directory/record behavior and an authorized reversible preferredName edit through the real UI and updateEmployeeProfile, producing two immutable audit rows. This materially advances ordinary administrator self-service, but it does not designate/train Taylor administrators, prove the complete Day-1 admin action set, activate password reset, or establish production readiness, so C1-ADMIN-01 remains OPEN.

PR #1820 / 5ddb9e4a materially extends the User Detail administration path in merged code: a trusted admin.principalAccess.read returns account status and active governed Role assignments with assignment ids; the screen can show one contextual Enable/Disable action, add non-privileged Roles additively, remove a specific assignment, and include those existing access events in Change History. Emulator proof covered authorization, additive multi-role behavior, removal by assignment id, account-status round trips, audit shapes, and preservation of the legacy securityRole mirror. The PR explicitly performed NO deployment, so this is code-level self-service evidence only; C1-ADMIN-01 remains OPEN pending deployed verification, complete Day-1 admin coverage, designated/trained Taylor administrators, and production readiness.

PRs #1822 / 51819f47, #1823 / d84389f4, and #1827 / 4396844e materially expand the merged Administration model beyond #1820: PostgreSQL-backed tenant policy persistence, provider-neutral principals and memberships, Admin-only policy commands/API, tenant-scoped Role assignment with database referential integrity and idempotence, editable Object and field CRED policy, custom Role/field administration, and versioned workflow definitions. #1827 browser acceptance proved persistence through the real API and PostgreSQL at 1440/1024/375. These PRs were merged despite stale DRAFT/DO NOT MERGE labels; at that point they were not yet deployed.

PR #1829 / 0c733704 supersedes the prior undeployed caveat for the newer policy stack with COMPLETE non-production technical acceptance: browser PASS at 375/1024/1440, no-code restart PASS, byte-identical persistence across restart, stable audit count during restart, and governed cleanup. The non-production frontend/API/PostgreSQL path is therefore operational evidence, not repository-only evidence. C1-ADMIN-01 remains OPEN because the gate still requires the agreed complete Day-1 administrator action set plus designated/trained Taylor administrators and production readiness; this acceptance does not constitute Taylor acceptance or production authorization.

PR #1839 / bbed7792 adds docs/training/administration-policy-and-access.md for the accepted non-production revision, covering Roles & Permissions, Objects, Users stored-role assignments, and Workflows. This satisfies the deployment-close training item for that bounded policy/access release, but it does not prove designated Taylor administrators have been trained or that every Day-1 Administration workflow is covered.

gates.name: Day-1 workflow readiness
gates.closeWhen: Every Day-1 workflow has passed its applicable governed functional, sandbox, North Star, and acceptance gates.
evidence: docs/design/north-star-migration-ledger.md

PR #1761 / a81e5b47: Certification formally closed with world 1.8.0, 1093/1093, final applied-inventory verifier 38/38 PASS, and bounded live Purchasing, Receiving, and Cycle Count evidence. The closeout explicitly does not claim production deployment or close transferred findings.
PR #1749 / 0d76bea9 originally proved the physical-consumption/on-hand defect: consumed stock remained available after use.

PR #1775 / f8708713 closes that defect in code through the canonical WORK_ORDER_CONSUMPTION movement and command-scoped source projection, with nine emulator proofs including receive 5 / consume 2 -> on-hand 3 / availability 3 and the warehouse-to-truck double-subtraction guard. No general technician inventory read was granted.

Sandbox release evidence on 2026-09-03 shows the applicable Functions estate was deployed after #1775, and the subsequently accepted dashboard ran on platform-sandbox at 50792fef, a descendant of the consumption fix. The original PHYSICAL_CONSUMPTION blocker is therefore CLOSED IN RUNNING SANDBOX BEHAVIOR, not merely closed in code. This does not establish production deployment.

PR #1763 / 5824df2a retired the remaining stock_locations client-direct reader and the Rules read arm in code. Legacy stock_locations documents remain inert pending separately authorized disposition; this is no longer an active runtime reader/writer dependency.
PR #1792 / c6589c06: My Dashboard Family 10 was CLOSED / OWNER ACCEPTED against live platform-sandbox commit 50792fef, with 23 modules fully classified and NOT_WIRED = 0.

PR #1800 / c6ad5b68: the dashboard corrective chain was live-verified on platform-sandbox Hosting 6b281cd5. My Dashboard remains CLOSED / OWNER ACCEPTED with its post-acceptance correctives live-verified, and Technician Dashboard Family 11 is CLOSED / OWNER ACCEPTED / LIVE VERIFIED. The closeout preserves the open technician self-goal-read authority question, the non-blocking inverted Work Order timestamp data-quality finding, and production remains untouched and unauthorized.
Existing governed authorization, certification, sandbox persona, scanner, service, dispatch, sales, and inventory evidence remains source-specific authority rather than being copied into this ledger.

PR #1762 / b19a7486: FIN-BLOCK-003A cost activation merged (Decision #166) — new purchase commitments require price + currency, legacy unpriced purchases grandfathered by a server-stamped priceAuthorityVersion, receipt produces immutable AcquisitionCostFact.

PR #1776 / 4c6b98c0 plus #1778 / 5b2bb0c6: EOS now supports governed financial-policy profiles with multiple tested costing strategies; sandbox configure/read authority is activated under the ruled access model and the lock is absolute. Taylor's actual deployment profile remains a customer/accounting choice and is not inferred here.

PR #1811 / c051af0c, PR #1813 / 32bd8270, PR #1814: Email Connections + Inbound Work. Base EOS takes an inbound email into a governed intake record and Accept creates exactly one Work Order without anyone retyping the message; real Microsoft Graph and Gmail transport, OAuth with PKCE and single-use state, refresh tokens held per connection in Secret Manager (never as Firestore fields), attachment bytes retrieved into a private bucket and served only through a governed callable; PR #1814 is the North Star pass over both surfaces. Deployed to platform-sandbox on 2026-09-06 as build de90d6b0 (Service ▸ Inbound Work fully operable; the connection actions are not, because the eight provider-transport Functions bind OAuth secrets that environment does not have and stay excluded from the deploy set). NO real mailbox bound (no non-production tenant credentials were available), Owner-accepted 2026-09-06 against build de90d6b0 (surfaces accepted; the capability is NOT closed - no training guide exists and no real mailbox is bound), and outbound email is not built. Production untouched and unauthorized.

gates.name: Production security and authority verification
gates.authority: Verenward + Owner for protected production actions
gates.closeWhen: Production Rules, Functions, capabilities, roles, protected actions, tenant boundaries, and audit behavior are verified from the production environment for Day-1 scope.
evidence: Repository and sandbox governance evidence exists; production evidence remains required.

PR #1752 / be1e5579: read-only production R-32 exposure census found zero exposed principals and zero writes/deploys. It also found production is barely using the governed access model: two RoleAssignments on one principal, no manager Roles, and no location scopes. This narrows one production exposure question but does not satisfy full Day-1 production identity/authority verification.

PR #1768 / 0dd5e104 and #1779 / 7c5c39dc: Reporting now has a distinct activation/adoption boundary. Production adoption of the approved 25-capability set is representable in repository configuration, but the work explicitly records it as not live production evidence.

PRs #1822 / 51819f47 and #1823 / d84389f4 add merged non-production security foundations: tenant-scoped PostgreSQL policy storage, provider-neutral identity, composite membership/Role referential integrity, one-time administrator bootstrap, additive/idempotent Role assignment, audit-on-mutation, tenant isolation, spoofed-tenant refusal, restart persistence, and an API that refuses production startup.

PR #1829 / 0c733704 provides live non-production acceptance evidence for that policy service: browser acceptance, service restart without code change, persistence across restart, and governed cleanup all passed. This materially removes the prior 'no Render/Vercel policy environment deployed' blocker for non-production, but C1-SECURITY-01 remains IN_PROGRESS because its close condition explicitly requires Day-1 production authority verification; no production security activation, Taylor acceptance, or final authorization is inferred.

gates.name: Day-1 training readiness
gates.closeWhen: Every Day-1 role/workflow has current training matching the deployed product, designated Taylor administrators are trained, and the permanent deployment training-close gate is operational.
evidence: docs/training/README.md
docs/training/PURCHASING_RECORD_PURCHASE_ORDER.md exists as a deployment-gated user guide for the governed purchase-order price-entry behavior; its completion state remains tied to live verification.
PR #1792 / c6589c06 originally closed docs/training/MY_DASHBOARD.md for My Dashboard against the Owner-accepted sandbox behavior.

PR #1800 / c6ad5b68: docs/training/MY_DASHBOARD.md is COMPLETE — LIVE VERIFIED against platform-sandbox commit 6b281cd5 and now explicitly covers both My Dashboard and Technician Dashboard, including the post-acceptance corrective chain. This closes training for those two dashboard surfaces only; it does not satisfy the all-Day-1-role/workflow close condition.

Training-close gap discovered 2026-09-05: PR #1804 deployed and live-verified the new Administration -> Data Import workflow at sandbox commit b533757a, and PR #1808 deployed/live-verified the Administration -> Users workflow at sandbox Hosting 8e90b41e, but the authoritative docs/training directory at that time had no Data Import or Taylor EOS Administrator/Administration Users guide. Day-1 applicability still depends on C1-SCOPE-01.

Email Connections + Inbound Work (PRs #1811, #1813, #1814, #1816) was deployed to platform-sandbox on 2026-09-06 as build de90d6b0, Owner-accepted the same day, and now carries docs/training/email-connections-and-inbound-work.md representing that build. TRAINING: COMPLETE, so the permanent close rule is satisfied for this release. The guide covers both Roles and names the four administration actions that are inoperable in that environment rather than teaching them.

PR #1839 / bbed7792 adds docs/training/administration-policy-and-access.md representing frontend 0c733704 and EOS API 44f423c9 after the non-production technical acceptance in PR #1829. It covers Roles & Permissions, Objects, Users stored-role assignments, and Workflows, and therefore satisfies the training-close item for that bounded Administration policy/access release. It does not cover Administration -> Data Import, does not establish training acceptance by designated Taylor administrators, and does not by itself close C1-TRAINING-01.

The remaining Administration training gap is narrower than previously recorded: Data Import still lacks a current guide, and Administration -> Users / User Detail behavior outside the stored-role-assignment panel must be checked against Day-1 scope and training coverage before closure.

gates.name: Cutover rehearsal and authorization package

gates.name: Customer 1 CI cost containment
gates.closeWhen: Ledger/documentation-only updates do not trigger broad application CI or GitHub Pages rebuilds, and no Windows-hosted Actions are used for ledger automation.
evidence: PR #1726 merged as 606278d2fcaf2aa26290d97d5c7f0f455c03dc9e; GitHub Pages is now path-filtered and remains ubuntu-latest.

Measured on docs-only Customer 1 reconciliation commit 72be6c52: no GitHub Pages deployment was triggered, but Vite Build Check and Operational Payload Guard still ran. Therefore the original READY claim was too broad and this gate is reopened until broad application CI is also excluded for ledger/training-only changes.

PR #1802 head d52dab2a changed exactly one docs/customer-1 charter file and still triggered Vite Build Check, Operational Payload Guard, and Secret scan. This independently confirms broad application CI isolation remains incomplete; no GitHub Pages or Windows-hosted runner evidence was observed.

PR #1839 head b870d7a1 changed exactly one docs/training file and still triggered Vite Build Check, Operational Payload Guard, and Secret scan. The Vite build job ran on ubuntu-latest. This is fresh confirmation that docs/training/** remains coupled to broad application CI; no Windows-hosted Action was introduced or observed.

gates.name: Final production dependency authorization
